QuestionQ101

Verified/Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture

Your company has chosen to create a backup replica of its on-premises user-authentication PostgreSQL database on Google Cloud Platform. The database is 4 TB, and substantial updates occur frequently. Replication requires communication over private address space.

Which networking approach should you use?

Explanation

Google Cloud Dedicated Interconnect provides direct private connectivity between an on-premises network and Google’s network and is designed to transfer large data volumes. Its high-capacity links are suitable for continuous replication of a 4 TB database with frequent large updates, whereas Cloud VPN tunnels have substantially lower per-tunnel bandwidth.

QuestionQ102

Verified/Ensuring solution and operations excellence

Your company has a Google Cloud project that uses BigQuery for data warehousing with pay-per-use pricing. You need to monitor queries in real time to identify the most expensive queries and the users who spend the most. What should you do?

Explanation

BigQuery audit logs record user activity, including jobs and queries. Exporting the relevant BigQuery Data Access logs to a BigQuery dataset through a Cloud Logging sink makes the log data available for SQL analysis by submitting user and billed query volume. Cloud Billing exports are intended for billing analysis and have variable reporting and export latency, so they do not provide the required real-time, per-user query monitoring.

QuestionQ103

Verified/Ensuring solution and operations excellence

For this question, refer to the KnightMotives Automotive case study. KnightMotives manages supplier data and pricing in a central MySQL database at headquarters (HQ). Only HQ personnel are permitted to modify the data. Each local plant maintains a copy of the data in its own MySQL database, often with a different database schema or version. Every night, a batch job exports any product or price changes from the central HQ database in XML format and stores the updated data on a central FTP server. Each local plant must download this XML file and update its local system with the new information. Data retained by some plants has become inconsistent with the source data because of XML parsing issues. HQ wants to easily confirm that every change is applied correctly at each plant.

Explanation

A Cloud SQL for MySQL primary can replicate to one or more external MySQL replicas. Standardizing the plant schemas and configuring their local databases as external read replicas replaces error-prone XML file processing with MySQL replication. Replication status, including whether a replica is caught up, can be checked with MySQL replication status, enabling HQ to verify that plant copies have applied the source changes correctly. Google Cloud: Configure external replicas

QuestionQ106

Verified/Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture

A large enterprise is developing a file-processing pipeline on Google Cloud. The pipeline receives raw files that a fleet of hundreds of Compute Engine virtual machines (VMs) in one region subsequently accesses for parallel processing. These VMs require concurrent, low-latency read and write access to a shared file system. You must implement a storage solution that provides the highest possible throughput to reduce the total processing time. What should you do?

Explanation

A Filestore Enterprise instance is a managed regional NFS file share that Compute Engine VMs can mount concurrently, providing a single shared file system with low-latency access. This meets the requirement for hundreds of VMs across one region, unlike object storage, separate zonal file systems, or multi-writer block storage that requires specialized coordination and is not intended as a directly shared general-purpose file system.

QuestionQ107

Verified/Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture

Your company has recently acquired another company with infrastructure in Google Cloud. Each company has its own Google Cloud organization. Both companies use a Shared Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) to provide network connectivity for their applications. Some subnets used by the two companies overlap. To integrate both businesses, the applications need private network connectivity. These applications are not on overlapping subnets. You want to provide connectivity with minimal re-engineering. What should you do?

Explanation

VPC Network Peering rejects peering configurations when subnet IP ranges overlap. Cloud VPN provides an IPsec connection between VPC networks and can be configured to carry traffic only for the non-overlapping application subnet ranges that require connectivity, avoiding an address-renumbering or instance-redeployment effort.

QuestionQ109

Verified/Designing for security and compliance

Your company uses Google Cloud. Under the Organization, you have two folders: Finance and Shopping. Development-team members belong to a Google Group, and that development-team group has the Project Owner role assigned at the Organization level. You need to prevent the development team from creating resources in projects within the Finance folder. What should you do?

Explanation

Google Cloud IAM allow-policy bindings inherit down the resource hierarchy, and the effective allow policy is the union of inherited and locally assigned roles. A Viewer role on Finance cannot override an Owner role inherited from the Organization. Remove the group’s Organization-level Owner binding and assign Owner only on the Shopping folder, so the role applies to Shopping projects but not Finance projects.

QuestionQ110

Verified/Designing for security and compliance

A BigQuery project contains several users. For auditing, you need to determine how many queries each user executed during the past month. What should you do?

Explanation

The project-level INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS view contains metadata for all BigQuery jobs in a project, including user_email, creation_time, and job_type. Filtering it to last-month QUERY jobs and grouping by user_email produces the per-user query counts; its job history retention covers the requested period.

QuestionQ111

Verified/Managing implementation

You are migrating an application that uses MySQL from on-premises to Google Cloud. The application will run on Compute Engine and use Cloud SQL. You want to cut over to the Compute Engine deployment with minimal downtime and without customer data loss. You also want to migrate the application with minimal modifications and determine the cutover strategy.

What should you do?

Explanation

Cloud SQL replication from an external MySQL server is designed to migrate self-managed MySQL data to Google Cloud with minimal downtime. Keeping the Compute Engine application connected to the on-premises database while Cloud SQL replicates preserves normal writes; after replication catches up, stopping the application, promoting the Cloud SQL replica to a standalone primary, and repointing the application provides a short, controlled cutover without data loss.

QuestionQ118

Verified/Ensuring solution and operations excellence

Your company plans to upload several important files to Cloud Storage. Once the upload is complete, they want to confirm that the uploaded content is identical to their on-premises copies. You want to minimize the cost and effort required for this verification. What should you do?

Explanation

Cloud Storage maintains a CRC32C checksum for every object. Computing CRC32C hashes for the on-premises files and comparing them with the uploaded objects’ CRC32C metadata verifies data integrity without incurring the time and retrieval cost of downloading the files or developing a custom hashing application.

QuestionQ120

Verified/Ensuring solution and operations excellence

The application reliability team at your company has added a debug feature to its backend service that sends all server events to Google Cloud Storage for later analysis. The event records are at least 50 KB and at most 15 MB, and they are expected to peak at 3,000 events per second. You want to minimize data loss.

Which process should you implement?

Explanation

Storing each event as a separate compressed object limits the loss from any individual failed upload. Including metadata in the object body ensures it is persisted with the event in the same write operation. Randomized object-name prefixes distribute high-volume writes more evenly; Cloud Storage recommends avoiding sequential names at high request rates because they can constrain performance.

QuestionQ121

Verified/Managing implementation

A financial-services company is retiring one of its on-premises data centers. As part of this effort, it must perform a one-time migration of 500 ТВ of historical transaction archives to a Cloud Storage bucket for long-term retention.

The data center’s 1 Gbps internet egress is shared with critical business operations. You must complete the secure data transfer within a 60-day window to meet the decommissioning deadline. What should you do?

Explanation

Transfer Appliance is designed for large on-premises transfers when available network bandwidth is limited or cannot safely meet the required deadline. Copying the archives to the appliance over the high-speed local network and shipping it to Google avoids saturating the shared 1 Gbps internet connection; Google then uploads the data to the Cloud Storage bucket. A 500 ТВ online transfer at 1 Gbps would consume nearly the entire 60-day period even at uninterrupted theoretical throughput.

QuestionQ125

Verified/Ensuring solution and operations excellence

You have a Compute Engine application that you want to autoscale when total memory utilization rises above 80%. You installed the Cloud Monitoring agent and configured the autoscaling policy as follows:

You notice that the application does not scale during high load. You want to fix this. What should you do?

Explanation

agent.googleapis.com/memory/percent_used reports separate time series for memory states such as used, buffered, cached, and slab. A filter joined with AND requires one time series to have every listed state simultaneously, which is impossible; therefore, it selects no usable series for autoscaling. Filtering on metric.label.state = 'used' selects the memory-in-use percentage, and GAUGE correctly compares its recent values with the utilization target of 80.

QuestionQ126

Verified/Designing for security and compliance

Mountkirk Games must build a repeatable, configurable method for deploying isolated application environments. Developers and testers may access each other’s environments and resources, but they must not access staging or production resources. The staging environment requires access to certain production services.

What should you do to isolate development environments from staging and production?

Explanation

In Google Cloud the project is the primary boundary for IAM and resource isolation. Putting development and test in one project lets developers and testers freely access each other's resources, while a separate project for staging and production denies them access to those environments. Because staging and production share a single project, staging can be granted access to the specific production services it needs. A separate network (B) or subnetwork (C) only isolates at the network layer, not at the IAM/resource level, and three separate projects (D) would needlessly complicate the required staging-to-production access.

QuestionQ131

Verified/Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture

You have been hired by your client to lead the migration of their application infrastructure to GCP. A current issue is that their on-premises high-performance SAN needs frequent, costly upgrades to keep pace with these identified workloads:

  • 20 TB of log archives kept for legal reasons
  • 500 GB of VM boot/data volumes and templates
  • 500 GB of image thumbnails
  • 200 GB of customer session-state data that lets customers restart sessions even after being offline for several days

Which option best represents your recommendations for a cost-effective storage allocation?

Explanation

Customer session state that must survive customers being offline for several days needs durable storage. Memcache can provide low-latency cached access, while Cloud Datastore persists the session data. Local SSD is temporary storage and may lose data when its VM stops, restarts, crashes, or is terminated; it also cannot be used as a boot device. Cloud Storage lifecycle rules can automatically transition or manage objects to reduce the cost of retained archives and other object data.

You need to deploy an application on Google Cloud. The application receives traffic over TCP and reads from and writes to the filesystem. It does not support horizontal scaling. Because concurrent access causes corruption, the application process needs exclusive control of the data on the filesystem. The business can accept downtime during an incident, but the application must be available 24/7 to support business operations.

You need to design this application's architecture on Google Cloud. What should you do?

Explanation

An active-passive pair in separate zones prevents concurrent access to the application data while retaining a standby for failover. A regional persistent disk synchronously replicates storage across two zones and can be attached to the standby VM during failover, which suits an application that permits incident downtime. A network load balancer supports TCP traffic; an HTTP load balancer does not provide the required TCP load-balancing architecture.

QuestionQ151

Verified/Designing for security and compliance

Company Overview –

Altostrat is a leading organization in the media industry, with an extensive audio and video collection comprising podcasts, interviews, news broadcasts, and documentaries. Its success in providing premium content to a diverse audience requires a content management system that can keep up with the dynamic media landscape.

Solution Concept –

Altostrat wants to modernize its content-management and user-engagement strategies with Google Cloud generative AI. It wants a platform that enables customers through personalized recommendations, natural-language interactions, and seamless self-service support. At the same time, it wants to increase revenue through dynamic pricing, targeted marketing, and personalized product suggestions.

The seamless integration of AI-powered tools into the existing Google Cloud environment will allow Altostrat to efficiently manage its vast media library, improve user experiences, and unlock new revenue streams. Google Cloud generative AI will reinforce its leadership in the media industry.

Existing Technical Environment –

Altostrat’s content management and delivery platform uses GKE for scalability and high availability, which are essential for handling its extensive media library. Its broad media library, covering various document, audio, and video formats, is stored in Cloud Storage. To obtain valuable insights into user behavior, content-consumption patterns, and audience demographics, Altostrat uses BigQuery as its primary data warehouse. It also uses Cloud Run functions for serverless execution of event-driven tasks such as video transcoding, metadata extraction, and personalized content recommendations.

Although Altostrat has made significant progress in cloud adoption, it also retains some legacy on-premises systems for specific workflows such as content ingestion and archival. These systems are planned for modernization and migration to Google Cloud in the near future. User management and authentication are currently managed through a combination of Google Identity and third-party identity providers. For monitoring and observability, Altostrat uses a mix of native Google Cloud tools, such as Cloud Monitoring, and open-source solutions, such as Prometheus, with alerts mainly sent through email notifications.

Business Requirements –

  • Accelerate and improve the reliability of operational workflows across all environments. [Google Cloud + On-premises]
  • Simplify infrastructure management for rapid application deployment.
  • Optimize cloud storage costs while preserving high availability and scalability for media content.
  • Enable natural-language interaction with the platform and 24/7 user support.
  • Automatically create concise summaries of media content.
  • Extract rich metadata from media assets using NLP and computer vision.
  • Detect and filter inappropriate content.
  • Analyze media content to identify trends and extract insights.
  • Inform content strategy and decision-making with data.

Technical Requirements –

  • Modernize CI/CD for containerized deployments using a centralized management platform.
  • Provide secure, high-performance hybrid-cloud connectivity for data ingestion.
  • Provide scalable, high-performing Kubernetes environments both on-premises and in the cloud.
  • Optimize cloud storage costs for increasing media volumes.
  • Design AI-powered detection of harmful content.
  • Ensure AI systems are auditable and their decisions are explainable.
  • Use LLMs and conversational AI for personalized experiences and content virality.
  • Develop advanced chatbots with natural-language understanding to deliver personalized assistance.
  • Provide automated summarization for diverse media.

Executive Statement –

At Altostrat, we are adopting the next frontier of artificial intelligence to transform our content strategy. By harnessing generative AI, we will deliver an unparalleled user experience by empowering our audience with intelligent tools for content discovery, personalized recommendations, and seamless interaction. Reliability and cost management are our highest priorities. This strategic initiative will deepen engagement, build customer loyalty, and unlock new revenue streams through targeted marketing and tailored content offerings. We envision a future in which AI-driven innovation is central to our business, leading to greater company success and exceptional value for our customers.

For this question, refer to the Altostrat Media case study. Altostrat keeps a large media-content library, including sensitive interviews and documentaries, in Cloud Storage. It is concerned with the confidentiality of this content and wants to prevent unauthorized access. Explanation

Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) use Cloud KMS with Cloud Storage, giving the organization control over key permissions, rotation, lifecycle, and protection settings while providing key-usage audit logs. Applying CMEK to buckets containing sensitive media and restricting bucket access through IAM roles and groups provides managed encryption with appropriate access control.

QuestionQ163

Verified/Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture

Your ecommerce platform runs a regional Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database that stores critical order information. The business requires a recovery time objective (RTO) of less than 10 minutes and a recovery point objective (RPO) of 2 minutes to maintain business continuity during a full regional outage. You must design a disaster-recovery strategy for the Cloud SQL database that satisfies the business's strict RTO and RPO requirements while avoiding operational complexity. What should you do?

Explanation

A cross-region Cloud SQL read replica provides a continuously replicated copy in a second region for regional disaster recovery. When the primary region is unavailable, promoting that replica creates a writable standalone primary in the surviving region, providing much faster recovery than backup restoration. Cross-region replication is asynchronous, so replication lag must remain within the 2-minute RPO target. High availability failover operates only between zones in the same region and does not protect against a complete regional outage.

A news-feed web service is running the following code on Google App Engine. At peak load, users report seeing news articles that they have already viewed. What is the most likely cause of this issue?

Explanation

The sessions dictionary is process memory local to one application instance, rather than shared persistent session storage. App Engine can scale to multiple instances and route consecutive requests from the same user to different instances; an instance that lacks the user’s prior in-memory state treats the viewed list as empty and returns previously viewed articles. QuestionQ177

Verified/Designing for security and compliance

Google Cloud Platform resources are organized hierarchically through organizations, folders, and projects. When Cloud Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies are set at these different levels, what is the effective policy at a specific node in the hierarchy?

Explanation

Google Cloud IAM allow policies propagate downward through the resource hierarchy. A resource’s effective allow policy is the union of the allow policy set on that resource and the allow policy inherited from its parent resources.

QuestionQ181

Verified/Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes

You use Cloud CDN to serve static HTTP(S) website content hosted on a Compute Engine instance group. You want to increase the cache hit ratio.

What should you do?

Explanation

For identical static content served through both HTTP and HTTPS, excluding the protocol from the Cloud CDN cache key allows requests using either protocol to use the same cached object. This avoids separate cache entries for the same resource and can raise the cache hit ratio.

For this question, use the TerramEarth case study. TerramEarth has chosen to store data files in Cloud Storage. You need to configure a Cloud Storage lifecycle rule to retain 1 year of data while minimizing file storage cost.

Which two actions should you take?

Explanation

Cloud Storage lifecycle management can change Standard objects to Coldline storage, and it can delete objects when they meet an age and storage-class condition. Moving objects to Coldline at 30 days minimizes ongoing storage cost; deleting Coldline objects at 365 days retains them for one year and exceeds Coldline's 90-day minimum storage duration.

QuestionQ183

Verified/Designing for security and compliance

A company has a networking team and a development team. The development team operates applications on Compute Engine instances containing sensitive data. The development team needs administrative permissions for Compute Engine. The company requires that the networking team manage all network resources. The development team does not want the networking team to access the sensitive data on the instances. What should you do?

Explanation

Shared VPC centralizes VPC network resources in a host project while allowing application resources, including Compute Engine instances, to reside in attached service projects. The Network Admin role on the host project manages network resources but does not grant administration of instances and disks in the service project, preserving separation from sensitive workload data. The development team can receive Compute Admin in the service project to manage its Compute Engine resources.

QuestionQ184

Verified/Analyzing and optimizing technical and business processes

Your company runs an application on Google Cloud that gathers data from thousands of globally distributed physical devices. Data is published to Pub/Sub and streamed in real time to an SSD Cloud Bigtable cluster through a Dataflow pipeline.

The operations team reports that the Cloud Bigtable cluster has a hotspot and that queries are taking longer than expected. You need to fix the issue and stop it from recurring. What action should you take?

Explanation

Cloud Bigtable row keys are lexicographically sorted, so a sequential or otherwise concentrated key pattern directs disproportionate reads or writes to a small key range and creates a hotspot. A row-key design that distributes keys evenly across the key space spreads workload across nodes and prevents the hotspot. Adding nodes does not fix a schema-driven hotspot when traffic remains concentrated on the same row or tablet range.

QuestionQ187

Verified/Designing for security and compliance

Your organization uses distinct Google Cloud projects for shared services, development, testing, and production.

  • The shared services project contains private CI/CD runners and a centralized Artifact Registry.
  • The development, testing, and production projects contain the GKE clusters on which applications are deployed.

You must design an architecture that lets the CI/CD runners connect to the GKE clusters and lets the clusters pull images from Artifact Registry, all through private IP addresses. Direct network traffic among the development, testing, and production environments must, however, be strictly prohibited. What should you do?

Explanation

A hub-and-spoke VPC Network Peering design gives each environment private internal connectivity to the shared-services VPC, allowing access to shared CI/CD and GKE-related resources. VPC Network Peering is not transitive, so environments peered only with shared services cannot communicate with one another through that VPC. Private GKE access to Artifact Registry can use private Google API access, including the restricted VIP configuration where required.

QuestionQ191

Verified/Ensuring solution and operations excellence

Your company operates a critical, revenue-producing ecommerce application served by a regional managed instance group (MIG) behind an external HTTP(S) Load Balancer. The operations team is currently overloaded with low-priority notifications and is beginning to ignore alerts. Your team's service level objective (SLO) is to maintain 99.9% availability, measured as the ratio of successful requests (2xx status codes) to total requests. You want to reduce noise from non-critical events and ensure that the team is notified only about actionable issues that threaten the SLO. What should you do?

Explanation

An error-budget burn-rate alert directly monitors the availability SLO and identifies when the allowed 0.1% failure budget is being consumed rapidly enough that the SLO is likely to be violated. Paging on projected exhaustion within 24 hours prioritizes incidents affecting user-observed service health, while avoiding noisy alerts for individual resource metrics, log entries, or instance-count changes that may not endanger availability.

QuestionQ194

Verified/Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture

Your company runs an enterprise application on Compute Engine that needs high availability and high performance. The application is deployed on two instances across two zones in the same region in active-passive mode. It writes data to a persistent disk. If a single zone fails, that data must be immediately available to the instance in the other zone. You want to maximize performance while minimizing downtime and data loss.

What should you do?

Explanation

Regional SSD Persistent Disk synchronously replicates every write between two zones in the same region, protecting against a single-zonal failure with minimal recovery point objective. During a zonal outage, force-attaching the regional disk to the standby instance in the surviving replica zone makes the replicated data available without waiting for snapshots or periodic file synchronization.

QuestionQ200

You are moving a critical on-premises inventory-management application to Google Cloud. The application is a monolith with a traditional relational database, and the immediate business objective is a rapid data-center exit. The monolith exposes an API to other business-critical applications.
